info.title: Screeps World socket API
info.description:
Community-maintained contract of the official Screeps World (screeps.com) socket protocol, not published by Screeps. One SockJS connection carries unframed text protocol lines, client commands and JSON channel events. Evidence: static analysis of the official web client assets (pinned by bust and SHA-256 in coverage.json), node-screeps-api and the official private-server source screeps/backend-local, pinned in sources.json/coverage.json and cited per message in `x-sources`, plus dated read-only observations of screeps.com (`x-observations`). `x-unverified` states evidence gaps.

Session: open the connection; the server greets with `time`, `protocol` and `package`; send `auth <token>` (the HTTP API token) and wait for `auth ok <token>`, which also returns the token to keep using; then `subscribe <channel>` for each channel. Optionally send `gzip on` to receive larger channel events compressed. Subscriptions belong to one connection: after reconnecting, authenticate and subscribe again. The official client reconnects after one second and resubscribes everything it had subscribed.

This document describes the server: `receive` operations are client commands and `send` operations are server messages. Standalone/private servers are described by the separate standalone compatibility profile (profiles/standalone.json, `socket`), not by this document. Subscribing is read-only, but a token grants full account access: never send it to an untrusted host.

screeps-com.description: SockJS endpoint configured as `https://screeps.com/socket/` in the official client. Clients without a SockJS library open a plain WebSocket to `wss://screeps.com/socket/websocket` (the SockJS raw WebSocket transport): every protocol line, command and event is exactly one text frame, without SockJS framing. Other SockJS transports wrap the same messages in SockJS frames.

socket.title: Socket connection
socket.description: The raw WebSocket transport of the SockJS endpoint; one connection multiplexes every message below. Channel events are JSON text `[channel, data]`; `err@<channel>` instead of `<channel>` marks an error event of that channel. Any channel event may arrive as a `gz:` compressed frame after `gzip on`. Text that starts with `[` is a channel event; everything else is a protocol line. Subscription channel names are case-sensitive and must be sent exactly as described by each event message.
